messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Does this functionality already exist?
parts:
I am dissatisfied with the current summary statistics for a data.frame.  I want to be able to specify the summary statistics for the table that I want computed not just the defaults for the class.  I came across this problem recently with creating a demographics table.  So I fixed it. 

 I created a function that can be passes to ldply and have functions specified as the extra arguments and produce a data frame with the summary statistics.  Functions must take a vector and return a vector.  Names can be optionally specified.  You can see it at  https://gist.github.com/1711802.  

I can't help but think this sort of thing probably already exists, but I could not find it, and it was just a few minutes to write up.  Aggregate gets close but not quite.  Either way it is a useful function for plyr.


Thanks,
Andrew

messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Re: Does this functionality already exist?
parts:
you might be interested in 

summarise()


require(plyr)
ddply(FAfinal, "gender", summarise, mean = mean(symmetry, na.rm = TRUE))
  gender        mean
1      1 -0.10718687
2      2  0.09220376

group <- c(rep('A', 8), rep('B', 15), rep('C', 6))
sex   <- sample(c("M", "F"), size=29, replace=T)
age   <- runif(n=29, min=18, max=54)
dfx   <- data.frame(group, sex, age)
 
# Note the use of the '.' function to allow 
# group and sex to be used without quoting
 
ddply(dfx, .(group, sex), summarize, 
    mean = round(mean(age), 2), 
    sd   = round(sd(age), 2)
)
 
#   group sex  mean    sd
# 1     A   F 35.89  8.53
# 2     A   M 38.01 15.09
# 3     B   F 39.08 10.79
# 4     B   M 37.38  9.55
# 5     C   F 30.01    NA
# 6     C   M 34.78 11.50
 
# An example using a formula for .variables
ddply(baseball[1:100,], .variables= ~year, .fun=nrow)
# Applying two functions; nrow and ncol
ddply(baseball, .(lg), c("nrow", "mean"))
# Calculate mean runs batted in for each year
 rbi <- ddply(baseball, .(year), summarise, 
   mean_rbi = mean(rbi, na.rm = TRUE))
# Plot a line chart of the result
plot(mean_rbi ~year, type="l", data=rbi))

messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Re: Does this functionality already exist?
parts:
It is a possible solution, but I see three problems with that solution.  here is what I came up with.

colwise(each(min, max))(mtcars)

problems:
  1. wrong oriantation, variables should be rows, due to possibly differing types, integer vs numeric vs string.
  2. does not allow for multiple values computed such as quantile.
  3. No names.  I know your hatred to row names, but you do need to identify the computed values.  adding the names is an extra step that could be omitted.

-Andrew
